H1.question: Do people spend a found break on more fun than a planned break?
H1.account: A found break goes to more fun than a planned break: the found-time effect of Chung and colleagues, in the pooled sample of 12 countries.

H2.question: Do people give AI-saved time to paid work more, or less, than found time?
H2.account: The work account: time saved when an assistant completes the work goes back to paid work more than time freed because the work was dropped.

H3.question: Do people spend AI-saved time on fun like a planned break?
H3.account: AI-saved time goes to fun like planned time, within the bound, as the work account predicts.

H4.question: Does labeling the saving change the share of fun videos, and in which direction?
H4.account: A named saving is treated as a gain: the label raises the share of fun.

H5.question: Do people spend AI-saved time on less fun than found time?
H5.account: The work account: AI-saved time goes to less fun than found time.

pair_h3_h5.account: AI-saved time goes to fun like planned time and to less fun than found time, as the work account predicts.
